correctness.rationale: The identity XY=R(X)×C(Y) makes squares precisely the rectangles and makes each fiber over a square intrinsic. On the rectangular band of idempotents, equality of all right products recognizes equal row support, and equality of all left products recognizes equal column support. Therefore the induced automorphism is a pair of independent index permutations. In each fiber, missing-row/missing-column inclusion-exclusion counts all incidence patterns with full support; subtracting its unique rectangle gives N. For v≥2, appending a full row injects the nonrectangular full-support u×v patterns into those on (u+1)×v. A pattern with one entry missing in the new row is full-support (both dimensions at least two) and is outside the image; hence the increase is strict. Appending full columns gives the needed weak monotonicity, and transposition gives the dual strictness. Thus the maximum nonrectangular fiber size over column supports is N_(|A|,b), which distinguishes the row cardinalities for b≥2. The dual maximum distinguishes the columns for a≥2. Conversely every cardinality-preserving pair can be lifted by arbitrary compatible bijections of the nonrectangles preserving the unique rectangle per fiber; these respect all products by the initial identity. Choosing a common indexing of nonrectangles at each pair of dimensions gives a homomorphic splitting and the stated permutation action, so the factorial order follows. Singleton rigidity follows from the support sizes (1,1); when a dimension is one the operation is one-sided zero, so arbitrary permutations work, including a singleton/nonsingleton transposition unless a=b=1. Independently enumerated nonrectangles with full support to obtain N_(1,2)=0, N_(2,2)=6, N_(2,3)=24 and N_(3,3)=264. In (2,2) the only nontrivial kernel factor is the invariant full-support fiber, so the semidirect product is direct and has order 2880. The supplied script was read, not executed. Its product routine uses the support identity directly, so checking it is not an independent verification of the multiplication identity or an exhaustive search of unrestricted candidate permutations; the proof establishes both the identity and exhaustiveness.
residual_risks: Applies to the nonempty power of a fixed finite rectangular band; no claim for inclusion/union automorphisms or infinite bands.

evidence: Liu–Tringali prove singleton preservation for inverse semigroups, while a rectangular band except 1×1 has noncommuting idempotents and is not inverse. Their introduction attributes global determination for completely simple and completely 0-simple semigroups to Tamura's 1986 results, notwithstanding the narrower-looking paper title. Retrieval for Tamura's 1984 rectangular-group paper was bibliographic only.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Global determination asserts existence of a base-semigroup isomorphism when power semigroups are isomorphic; it does not say that a particular isomorphism restricts to one on singletons, much less enumerate all automorphisms. The inverse theorem cannot be applied merely because rectangular bands are regular. The 1984 paper is potentially more directly relevant but not readable from the inspected links.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Once cardinality rigidity is known, lifting, splitting by fiber labels and taking factorials are routine. The structural description alone does not decide what support permutations preserve sizes: the monotonicity/max argument uses the actual rectangular incidence counts. That step also explains why the one-sided boundary differs rather than merely supplying a renamed form of the decomposition.

originality.rationale: The rectangular-band/null-fiber decomposition and general power-semigroup reconstruction questions are prior; they should not be credited as new. The supported distinct claim identifies the size classes of both projections intrinsically, giving the exact automorphism group/order and sharp singleton-rigidity boundary for all finite rectangular bands. The strongest accessible earlier passages do not establish the needed support-size rigidity. The later indexed endomorphism classification materially overlaps the general fiber-map description and is explicitly compared below. Access to the strongest older primary candidates remains incomplete; pass is to the best of present evidence, not a claim of absolute priority.
residual_risks: The 1968, 1984 and 1986 primary texts were not fully accessible. In particular a more explicit automorphism or cardinality statement in Tamura 1984 could change the priority assessment.
The later catalogue record's unnamed earlier automorphism result was not resolved to a source; the later classification's actual overlap is credited.

value.rationale: The theorem recovers two support cardinalities from multiplication alone even though the automorphisms need not preserve an element's size or inclusion. This yields a complete exact group and a sharp nontrivial singleton-preservation boundary outside the inverse case. The boundary and intrinsic recovery explain why the result is more than a recount of the smallest group or a restatement of the null-fiber structure.
residual_risks: No implication is claimed for rectangular groups with nontrivial group factor or for broader Rees matrix semigroups.
